phase3_findings.description: The '(no engine-file read found in the supplied corpus)' headline in render_text conflates a genuine established zero with an unmeasurable corpus (every session file unreadable/escaped). Mitigated: skip tally surfaces unreadable_file/escaped_path counts. Suggest making the headline conditional on the skip tally.

Files under a symlinked subdirectory inside the corpus are silently not walked (os.walk followlinks=False). Fail-safe and correct in practice; suggest a one-line comment noting the intentional non-descent so it is not 'fixed' into followlinks=True (which would reopen the escape hole).

7-line descriptive block comment in lib/test/run.sh mostly enumerates what the focused test asserts; exceeds the three-line prevention-only cap. Only its last line ('INVOKES the test, not the script') is load-bearing. Borderline/undecidable — mirrors the adjacent #1209 block style.
Four-line inline comment on non-finite float / int(inf) OverflowError handling exceeds the three-line cap and is near-duplicated in the test file. Accurate and prevention-oriented; borderline.

render_text skip-rendering branch (## Skipped records / ## Dropped from an axis) is never exercised: all render assertions run against a zero-skip corpus. AC5's 'still produces a report' is verified at eval_corpus tuple level, not rendered-output level. One render_text assertion over a corpus with a malformed and an unresolvable-read-path record would close it.
main() is never driven end-to-end with a corpus containing skips, so no test proves the CLI returns 0 and emits a full report when malformed records are present (literal AC5 wording).

The source-path fallback in _context_identity (record lacking both sessionId and agentId, keyed on 'file:'+source) is unreached by any fixture/unit test; a regression dropping the fallback would collapse such records silently.
aggregate total_usage_missing_turns asserted only for presence, not numeric value against a usage-less corpus. Low value; per-context usage_missing implicitly exercised.

Two (arguably three) representations of 'unmeasured': ContextAccumulator.peak None internally vs UNESTABLISHED string externally vs usage_missing_turns count, producing a polymorphic public field peak_context: int|str whose int/str disjointness invariant is enforced nowhere structurally (aggregate relies on != UNESTABLISHED). Fragility, not a defect.

Untyped stringly-keyed dict contracts (per-context result, engine_files bucket, summary, report) flow between eval_corpus/aggregate/render_text/build_report despite __future__ annotations; key drift is a runtime KeyError/silently-wrong count rather than a static error. TypedDict/dataclass would self-document.

ContextAccumulator reaches into caller-owned skip tally via hard-coded key skipped['unresolvable_read_path'] += 1 with an unstated must-be-pre-seeded precondition (held only by new_skip_tally construction convention). Cleaner: accumulator owns its own counter and eval_corpus sums it.
main() error message 'transcript directory not found' is inaccurate when the path exists but is a file (os.path.isdir false). Behavior (exit 2, path named) is correct; wording only.
AC7 test exercises a symlinked file escape but not a symlinked directory escape (safe only via implicit os.walk followlinks=False). Adding a symlinked-directory-escape case would pin AC7 fully.
